# std.sparse

Sparse table: \(O(1)\) range folds of a fixed array (range minimum query, RMQ).

In prelude (no `use` needed): `SparseTable`.

## `struct SparseTable<D, T>(op: (T, T) -> T)`

`SparseTable<V, Int>(min, a)`: built in \(O(n \log n)\) time and memory, `fold` is \(O(1)\).

Fields: `n: Int`, `table: List<T>`.

- `fn new(op: (T, T) -> T, a: [D]T) -> SparseTable<D, T>` — \(O(\lvert D \rvert \log \lvert D \rvert)\) time and memory, `op` called \(O(\lvert D \rvert \log \lvert D \rvert)\) times; Build a sparse table for the idempotent, associative `op` over the values of `a`.; traps: never (a non-idempotent or non-associative `op` gives unspecified folds; check with `idempotent`)
- `fn fold(self, r: Range<D>) -> T` — \(O(1)\); The fold of `op` over the positions of the non-empty range `r`, as two overlapping power-of-two windows combined with one `op` call.; traps: when `r` is empty or reaches outside `D`
- `fn try_fold(self, r: Range<D>) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The fold of `r` like `fold`, or `None` when `r` is empty.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `D`
- `fn get(self, i: D) -> T` — \(O(1)\); The original value at position `i` (level 0 of the table).; traps: when `i` is outside `D`
- `@get fn all(self) -> T` — \(O(1)\); The fold of every position of `D`; `fold(D.all)`.; traps: when `D` is empty

## `struct DisjointSparseTable<D, T>(op: (T, T) -> T)`

Disjoint sparse table: \(O(n \log n)\) build and memory, \(O(1)\) range fold for ANY associative operation — no idempotence and no inverse required (matrix products, `Mod<P>` products, `MaxSub`, string concatenation).

Fields: `n: Int`, `table: List<T>`.

- `fn new(op: (T, T) -> T, a: [D]T) -> DisjointSparseTable<D, T>` — \(O(\lvert D \rvert \log \lvert D \rvert)\) time and memory, `op` called \(O(\lvert D \rvert \log \lvert D \rvert)\) times; Build a disjoint sparse table for the associative `op` over `a`.; traps: never (a non-associative `op` gives unspecified folds)
- `fn fold(self, r: Range<D>) -> T` — \(O(1)\), at most one `op` call; The fold of `op` over the non-empty range `r`, left to right in domain order, so a non-commutative `op` sees its operands in position order.; traps: when `r` is empty or reaches outside `D`
- `fn try_fold(self, r: Range<D>) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The fold of `r` like `fold`, or `None` when `r` is empty.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `D`
- `fn get(self, i: D) -> T` — \(O(1)\); The original value at position `i`.; traps: when `i` is outside `D`
- `@get fn all(self) -> T` — \(O(1)\); The fold of every position of `D`, left to right; `fold(D.all)`.; traps: when `D` is empty

## `struct SparseTable2D<R, C, T>(op: (T, T) -> T)`

\(O(\lvert R \rvert \cdot \lvert C \rvert \cdot \log \lvert R \rvert \cdot \log \lvert C \rvert)\) build and memory; \(O(1)\) rectangle fold for any associative, idempotent operation (`min`, `max`, `gcd`, `&`, `\|`).

Fields: `table: List<T>`, `h: Int`, `w: Int`, `lr: Int`, `lc: Int`.

- `fn new(op: (T, T) -> T, a: [R, C]T) -> SparseTable2D<R, C, T>` — \(O(\lvert R \rvert \lvert C \rvert \log \lvert R \rvert \log \lvert C \rvert)\) time and memory; Build a 2-D sparse table for the idempotent, associative `op` over the grid `a`: one `SparseTable` level per power-of-two row height and column width.; traps: never (a non-idempotent `op` gives unspecified folds)
- `fn fold(self, rows: Range<R>, cols: Range<C>) -> T` — \(O(1)\); The fold of `op` over the rectangle `rows` by `cols`, both non-empty: four overlapping power-of-two blocks combined with `op`.; traps: when either range is empty or reaches outside its domain
- `fn try_fold(self, rows: Range<R>, cols: Range<C>) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The rectangle fold like `fold`, or `None` when `rows` or `cols` is empty.; traps: when a range reaches outside its domain on a non-empty rectangle
- `fn get(self, r: R, c: C) -> T` — \(O(1)\); The original cell value `a[r, c]`.; traps: when `r` is outside `R` or `c` is outside `C`

## `struct LinearRmq<D, T>(before: (T, T) -> Bool)`

\(O(\lvert D \rvert)\) build and memory; \(O(1)\) range min/max query via block-of-64 bitmask RMQ (Four Russians).

Fields: `n: Int`, `vals: List<T>`, `mask: List<U64>`, `nb: Int`, `top: List<Int>`.

- `fn new(a: [D]T, before: (T, T) -> Bool = (x, y) => x <y) -> LinearRmq<D, T>: let vals = [a[i] for i in D] let n = vals.len let nb = (n + 63) / 64 var q = LinearRmq<D, T>(before, n, vals, [], nb, []) for b in 0..nb: var cur: U64 = U64(0) for i in 64 * b..min(64 * b + 64, n): while cur != U64(0) and before(q.vals[i], q.vals[64 * b + bit_width(cur) - 1]): cur ^= U64(1) <<(bit_width(cur) - 1) cur |= U64(1) <<(i - 64 * b) q.mask.push(cur)` — \(O(\lvert D \rvert)\) time and memory; Build a linear-space range-best structure over `a`, where `before(x, y)` means `x` is better than `y` (default `<`, so the best is the minimum).; traps: never (`before` must be a strict weak order, or results are unspecified)
- `fn argbest(self, r: Range<D>) -> D` — \(O(1)\); The position of the best element of the non-empty range `r` under `before`; the leftmost when several are equally best (neither is `before` the other).; traps: when `r` is empty or reaches outside `D`
- `fn best(self, r: Range<D>) -> T` — \(O(1)\); The value of the best element of the non-empty range `r` under `before`; `a[argbest(r)]`.; traps: when `r` is empty or reaches outside `D`
- `fn try_best(self, r: Range<D>) -> ?T` — \(O(1)\); The value of the best element of `r` like `best`, or `None` when `r` is empty.; traps: when a non-empty `r` reaches outside `D`

## Functions

- `fn idempotent<T>(op: (T, T) -> T, xs: List<T>) -> Bool` — \(O(n)\) calls of `op`; Whether `op(x, x) == x` for every sample `x` in `xs`: the law a sparse table needs on top of associativity.; traps: never (`op` may trap)

## Example

```cp
domain I = 0..5
let sp = SparseTable<I, Int>(min, [4, 2, 7, 1, 5])
print(sp.fold(I(0)..I(3)), sp.fold(I(2)..=I(4)))
// output: 2 1
```
